title: Edge rollup & trace-fanout gateway for VPC/On-prem observability
creator: Diego Martinez
description: Build a tenant-aware telemetry gateway to sit at the perimeter of Dedicated and Private deployments (VPC & on-prem). The gateway will terminate mutual TLS, authenticate/translate tenant tokens, perform lightweight rollups/aggregation for metrics, shard and fan out traces to internal collector pools, and enforce isolation constraints (no cross-tenant aggregation of raw traces). This ticket covers design, implementation of the gateway binary, ingress buffering/backpressure, tenant header translation, idempotent dedupe for span submissions, and integration with RBAC & KMS for tenant secrets. The goal is to reduce per-tenant ingest costs, improve SLOs for tail latency on the observability ingestion path, and prevent noisy neighbors from impacting other tenants in co-located Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway accepts mTLS client certs and falls back to signed opaque token for non-mTLS flows
Per-tenant routing header is normalized and recorded on all spans/metrics without exposing other tenants' identifiers
Adaptive rollup applied: metrics above configurable cardinality thresholds are rolled up with reason code and not forwarded raw
Fanout to internal collectors succeeds with at-least-once semantics and idempotent span dedupe for duplicates within 30s window
Backpressure and buffer utilization metrics exposed; gateway returns explicit 429 with retry-after when internal queues exceed thresholds
End-to-end integration tests for single-tenant and multi-tenant ingestion demonstrating isolation (no cross-tenant leakage)
Dashboard panels added: ingest p50/p95 latency, dropped spans/sec, buffer utilization, tenant-level ingress RPS, backpressure events
design_notes: Core design: lightweight edge binary written in Go that performs TLS termination and token validation (KMS-backed). Use a two-path pipeline: fast-path for validated, low-cardinality metrics (pass-through) and rollup-path for high-cardinality metrics (hash-based binning + semantic suffix aggregation). Traces are annotated with an internal tenant-id header and sharded by tenant to collector pools to preserve isolation; use a stable hashing ring to minimize re-shards on topology change. Deduplication uses a bloom-filter-backed in-memory window and a compact sync to redis for cross-instance duplicate suppression in dedicated clusters. Trade-offs: in-memory dedupe reduces storage I/O but may miss cross-instance duplicates during full cluster restart. We prefer eventual consistent semantics with at-least-once delivery and idempotent ingestion at collectors. Security: tenant secrets are fetched from KMS cache; mTLS and token flows require periodic key rotation. Observability: expose detailed self-metrics and traces for the gateway itself and emit structured events on policy rejections. Rollout: staged Canary in Dedicated region us-west-2 for 48h with synthetic traffic and tenant sampling, then opt-in for smaller Private customers before full rollout.
tasks: Proto: gateway gRPC/HTTP API and config schema
Implement mTLS termination, client cert mapping to tenant ID
Token translator: map opaque tokens to tenant metadata via KMS-backed auth service
Implement metrics rollup engine and cardinality thresholds config
Implement trace fanout with shard-ring and at-least-once delivery
Backpressure & persistent on-disk queue for graceful pressure handling
Deduplication window with redis-backed cross-instance sync
Add gateway self-metrics and structured logs; wire to Console dashboards
